---
title: "How do I calculate the expected value of a discrete probability distribution?"
---

## What the question asks

How do I calculate the expected value of a discrete probability distribution?

## Steps in RStudio

1. List each possible numeric outcome with its probability.

2. Check all probabilities are valid and total 1.

3. Multiply outcomes by probabilities and sum.

## Runnable example

```{r}
outcomes <- 0:3
p <- c(0.2,0.4,0.3,0.1)
stopifnot(all(p>=0),isTRUE(all.equal(sum(p),1)))
expectation <- sum(outcomes*p)
variance <- sum((outcomes-expectation)^2*p)
print(c(expected=expectation,variance=variance))
```

## Interpret the result

The expected value is 1.3 and the modeled variance is 0.81. Expected value is a long-run average, not necessarily a possible single outcome.

## Check before using your own data

All probabilities must be nonnegative and sum to 1; missing outcome probabilities cannot simply be assumed zero.
